conventions: Wisdom substantives completed by a supplied generic noun are headed on the word carrying the lexeme throughout this chapter, under rule 31: `מֵישָׁרִים` → *right things* (23.16), `זָר` → *strange things* and `תַּהְפֻּכֹות` → *perverse things* (23.33), `חָכָם` → *a wise child* (23.24), `נׇכְרִי` → *a foreign woman* (23.27), `זָלַל` → *gluttonous eaters* (23.20, beside the bare *the glutton* the ASV writes for the same lemma in 23.21). The one contested member is `מִמְסָךְ` → *mixed wine* (23.30), headed on *mixed*; *wine* was named as the competing head, because rule 31's tie-break reads the ASV's bare *wine* for `יַיִן` standing in that same verse as evidence that *wine* is a class noun rather than a supplied generic. A later reader revisiting the family should start there and nowhere else.

Where the ASV recasts a construct nominal of possession or quality as an English head noun with a clause of having, the supplied antecedent, the relative and the possessive verb all join that nominal's own unit and none of them is `added`: `בַּעַל נֶפֶשׁ` → *be a man given to appetite* gives *be a man given* to `בַּעַל`, headed on *given* because the possession is what that noun's own lexeme names (rule 43's closing paragraph), and `רַע עָיִן` → *of him that hath an evil eye* gives *of him that hath … evil* to `רַע`, headed on *evil* because the adjective's own lexeme is written (rules 19, 31, 46). This extends rule 43's `בַּעַל` carve-out to a construct chain headed by a quality word rather than a noun of ownership; the competing reading, marking the *hath* `added` under rule 43's count, was rejected because the whole English expression is one nominal's recasting and no clause stands in the Hebrew beside it.
report: Worked all 41 candidate lemma groups; none is a split. Every two-treatment bucket resolves to a word the ASV wrote differently: לְ and בְּ take the word written for them (23.3 *of*, 23.12 *to*/*unto*, 23.22 *unto*, 23.13/23.14 *with*) and go unrepresented exactly where the ASV promotes the object or writes no preposition (23.6, 23.9, 23.17, 23.26, 23.30) under rule 40; כִּי takes *For*, *when*, or the *For if* pair of 23.13; the waw takes *And*, *and*, *Or*, *Yea*, *But*, *Seeing* off the page and is unrepresented once (23.5); the article takes *the* wherever one is written and nothing where none is.

The two identical Vqrmsa שָׁכַב participles of 23.34 are one construction: *he that lieth down* and *he that lieth* differ only because the ASV wrote the particle once, and there is nothing to place in the second. The nearest thing to a real split is the phrasal particle — *vomit up* (23.8), *seek out* (23.30) and *lieth down* (23.34) join their verbs while *down* (23.31) is `added`. Rule 44 runs its subtraction on the source lexeme, and *goeth* already writes the hithpael of הָלַךְ while *vomit*, *seek* and *lieth* do not write קִיא, חָקַר and שָׁכַב whole (cf. rule 44's own *find out*), so the source licenses the difference. No patch.

Audited all 13 `added` units. Each is English supplied into a colon holding no morpheme that answers to it: the subject nouns *riches* (23.5) and *a man* (23.21), the object pronouns *it* (23.23, 23.35), the supplied clause *shalt thou say* (23.35), the relatives written over finite clauses juxtaposed to written antecedents (23.5 t020, 23.8 t003), the connectives *Yea* (23.23) and the two *and*s (23.35), and the *When* opening the third asyndetic colon of 23.31. Italics were treated as evidence only: 23.13's italic *For* went to כִּי and 23.17's italic *be* to the prepositional predicate, leaving only *thou* added.

Checked the two families this chapter could most easily have split and did not: an explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English while the copula goes to the predicate in all six verbless clauses (23.2, 23.3, 23.7, 23.11, 23.14, 23.19, 23.28), and a preposition the English verb needs to reach a bare object stays with the verb in 23.21 (*clothe … with*), 23.26 (*let delight in*) and 23.31 (*Look … upon*) while an adverbial accusative keeps its supplied word in 23.5 (*toward heaven*) and 23.32 (*At the last*).

BSB: 17 disagreements, none an error. Fourteen are documented convention differences — the rule 40 recastings that leave לְ/בְּ nothing (23.5, 23.6, 23.9, 23.17, 23.26, 23.30), the paragogic he of 23.12 and 23.26 (rule 32), the agreement article of 23.8 (rule 47), and articles the ASV simply does not write (23.5, 23.8). The remaining three are direct readings of the ASV: 23.8's suffixes (*The morsel*, object fronted) and 23.31's עֵינוֹ, left unrendered because *sparkleth* carries only יִתֵּן and rule 30's contiguity condition is broken by בַּכּוֹס.

One judgment a later reader may want to revisit, left as accepted: 23.30 heads מִמְסָךְ → *mixed wine* on *mixed* under rule 31's subtraction, and the verse names *wine* as the competing head. Rule 31's tie-break paragraph points the other way, since the ASV writes a bare *wine* for יַיִן in that same verse, which is the JOB.4.10-11 configuration. The naive subtraction does not clearly tie (*mixed* alone names nothing, *wine* alone is any wine), the word occurs twice in the OT, and I would not overturn a noted head choice on that footing.
